title: Module pullback exists in a universe containing both sites
statement: Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be categories whose objects and morphisms belong to a universe $W$ [def-weil-size-convention], with Grothendieck topologies $J,K$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Let $U:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be continuous. Let $R$ be a sheaf of rings on $(\mathcal C,J)$ and $S$ a sheaf of rings on $(\mathcal D,K)$, with section rings in $W$, and let $a:R\to U_*S$ be a ring-sheaf morphism. On categories of module sheaves with section modules in $W$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], the direct-image functor defined by restriction along $U$ and scalar restriction along $a$ has a left adjoint. The site-object and site-morphism universes may be strictly smaller than $W$. Neither preservation of finite limits nor preservation of coverings by $U$ is required.

proof.text: The free module on the lifted representable at X corepresents sections at X, by the free-module adjunction and lifted Yoneda. Hence direct image has a partial left adjoint there, with value the free module at U(X).

Form the coproduct of free lifted representables indexed by all sections of a module presheaf M. Evaluation at the identity gives a sectionwise surjective map to M. Present its kernel by another such coproduct. The resulting cokernel is M. All indices lie in W. Closure of the domain of a partial left adjoint under coproducts and cokernels, using Mathlib Functor.leftAdjointObjIsDefined_of_isColimit, proves existence of the presheaf left adjoint.

Pass to a small model of D in the coefficient universe and use Mathlib hasSheafifyEssentiallySmallSite for additive sheafification. Use GrothendieckTopology.WEqualsLocallyBijective.ofEssentiallySmall for its locally-bijective criterion. Mathlib SheafOfModules.PullbackConstruction.adjunction then composes presheaf pullback with module sheafification to give the required sheaf-module adjunction. All these arguments are made directly from Mathlib; no K-flat-complex module is imported.
